title: How do you build a training matrix for an accounting firm?
seoTitle: Training matrix for an accounting firm
description: Build an accounting firm training matrix: service lines against AML, client data security and privacy duties by market, with refresh rules and evidence.
shortAnswer: An accounting firm training matrix is built around service lines rather than job grades: tax and structuring, bookkeeping and client money, company secretarial, advisory and audit each carry different anti-money laundering exposure, and tax and bookkeeping teams also hold large volumes of client financial data. For each service line and market, the matrix records the obligation, the frequency, any event trigger and the evidence that shows staff can apply the rule, not just that they attended.
keyTakeaways: Map service lines, not grades: in Australia, creating trusts, holding client money and providing registered office addresses are regulated AML/CTF services, while routine compliance work may not be.
A practice that only arranges services under an AFS license may be exempt from AML training, but it loses that position as soon as it creates trusts or holds client money for transactions.
US tax preparation firms fall under the FTC Safeguards Rule, which requires security awareness training for all personnel even where the small institution exemption applies.
Client data duties differ by market: GDPR, Japan's APPI and the UAE data protection law imply training through security and supervision duties rather than naming a course.
Auditors, accountants and tax advisors are obliged entities under the EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation, which applies from July 10, 2027.

sections.heading: Why should an accounting firm organize its matrix by service line?

blocks.text: Because the same accountant can be inside or outside a regulated activity depending on the engagement, and the training duty follows the activity. Australia's tranche 2 reforms illustrate this: the Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre (AUSTRAC) regulates services listed in table 6 of the AML/CTF Act, and those services are profession neutral, so a tax partner who sets up a family trust is in scope for that engagement and a colleague preparing individual returns may not be.

The method in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) applies with one adjustment: before choosing rows, list the services the firm actually provides in each office, then attach roles to those services. A [skills matrix](/glossary/skills-matrix) built on job titles alone cannot show a supervisor which engagements create which duties.

sections.heading: Which accounting service lines carry which obligations?

blocks.text: Start with the AML exposure of each service line, then add the data security and privacy layer that applies to all of them. The table links each line to the Australian table 6 items AUSTRAC lists, as one market example; other markets define scope differently.

sections.heading: Which obligations apply to accounting firms in each market?

blocks.text: The obligation columns come from the library's regulation pages for each market. The summaries below use only those pages, and every link opens the full requirement.

items: **Australia.** Accounting practices providing table 6 services are reporting entities from July 1, 2026, and AUSTRAC's national risk assessment found services provided by accountants pose a high money laundering risk ([AML/CTF tranche 2 for lawyers and accountants](/regulations/aml-ctf-tranche-2-lawyers-accountants-training)). Section 5-9 of the AML/CTF Rules 2025 requires initial and ongoing training appropriate to each person's function and risks, and section 5-8 requires an assessment of skills, knowledge and integrity ([AUSTRAC AML/CTF training](/regulations/austrac-aml-ctf-training-requirements)). The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) counts staff training as an organizational measure under APP 11 ([Privacy Act staff training](/regulations/privacy-act-staff-training-requirements)).

**United States.** The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Safeguards Rule names tax preparation firms among the financial institutions it covers. Section 314.4(e) requires security awareness training for all personnel, updated to reflect the firm's risk assessment, plus security updates and training for information security staff ([FTC Safeguards Rule](/regulations/ftc-safeguards-rule-employee-training)).

**European Union and Portugal.** The EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation (AMLR) lists auditors, accountants and tax advisors among obliged entities. From July 10, 2027, Article 12 requires specific, ongoing, documented training, Article 9 a written training policy approved by the management body, and Article 13 an assessment of skills, knowledge and integrity ([EU AMLR](/regulations/eu-amlr-training-requirements)). Until then, Portuguese auditors and accountants in covered activities follow Article 55 of Law 83/2017 ([Portugal AML law](/regulations/portugal-aml-law-training-requirements)). The GDPR's data protection officer monitors awareness raising and training under Article 39 ([GDPR staff training](/regulations/gdpr-staff-training-requirements)).

**Japan.** Articles 23 and 24 of the Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI) require security control measures and supervision of employees who handle personal data, and the Personal Information Protection Commission's guidelines make employee education mandatory ([APPI employee training](/regulations/japan-appi-employee-training)). The Financial Services Agency's AML/CFT Guidelines expressly exclude certified public accountants and audit firms (Article 2(2) item 48), so a Japanese practice should not use them as its benchmark ([FSA AML/CFT Guidelines](/regulations/japan-fsa-aml-cft-guidelines-training)).

**United Arab Emirates.** Independent accountants and company and trust service providers are designated non-financial businesses and professions when carrying out the listed activities. Article 21(5) of Cabinet Resolution No. 134 of 2025 requires periodic programs and workshops ([UAE AML/CFT](/regulations/uae-aml-cft-training-requirements)). Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 has no express training article, but Article 7 requires appropriate technical and organizational measures and a record of who may access personal data ([UAE PDPL](/regulations/uae-pdpl-staff-training)).

sections.heading: What scope decisions must accounting staff be trained to make?

blocks.text: Staff who open engagements must be able to decide whether a service is regulated, because a misclassified engagement skips customer due diligence entirely. These decisions are judgment calls, so the training should be assessed on realistic engagement scenarios rather than recall questions.

items: **The bookkeeper test.** AUSTRAC works through a bookkeeper processing routine payments as an item 3 example. Whether payments are reasonably incidental to a non designated service decides whether the engagement is in scope.

**The business test.** A service counts even if provided once, alongside other work, or free to further the business, so occasional favors for long standing clients are not automatically outside scope.

**The item 54 position.** A business whose only designated service is arranging another designated service under an Australian financial services license is exempt from personnel due diligence and training, but must still enroll, assess risk, conduct initial due diligence and report suspicious matters. An accounting practice that also creates trusts or holds client money for transactions loses that position.

**Privilege is not available.** AUSTRAC recommends that non lawyers seek legal advice before withholding information on privilege grounds, which means accountants need an escalation route, not a privilege module.

blocks.text: Recording these decisions as assessment evidence connects to the distinction in [completion tracking vs competency verification](/compare/completion-tracking-vs-competency-verification).

sections.heading: How should client data security training be scoped in an accounting firm?

blocks.text: Scope it to everyone with access to client financial records, including seasonal, contract and outsourced staff, and tie its content to the firm's own risk assessment. Several of the linked rules define the trained population broadly and none of them lets a firm skip training because it is small.

items: **United States.** The FTC Safeguards Rule exempts institutions holding data on fewer than 5,000 consumers from 314.4(b)(1), (d)(2), (h) and (i) only, so paragraph (e) training duties still apply. Notification events involving at least 500 consumers must be reported to the FTC within 30 days of discovery, and discovery counts from the first day any employee knew, which makes recognizing and escalating an incident part of every employee's training.
**Japan.** The APPI definition of employee covers regular, contract, part time and dispatched workers and also directors and auditors, so seasonal staff belong on the matrix.

**European Union.** GDPR Articles 29 and 32(4) mean anyone acting under the firm's authority processes personal data only on instructions; infringing Articles 25 to 39 can attract fines of up to EUR 10 million or 2% of worldwide annual turnover.

**United Arab Emirates.** The PDPL does not apply to free zone companies with their own data protection legislation, such as those in DIFC and ADGM, so an Abu Dhabi office needs to confirm which regime its entity sits under before choosing content.

**Australia.** The small business exemption threshold is $3 million annual turnover with listed exceptions, and the privacy page lists AML/CTF reporting entities among covered entities, so a small practice that becomes a reporting entity should recheck its position.

sections.heading: How often should accounting firm training be repeated?

blocks.text: Mostly on a cycle the firm sets and documents, because almost none of the accounting rules fixes an interval. The firm should state its chosen cycle per row, the reasoning behind it and the events that force an earlier refresh.

items: **Stated or exemplified intervals.** AUSTRAC's good practice example runs refreshers at least annually or on significant change; its general guidance gives 12 months for customer facing staff and 6 to 12 months for compliance officers and senior management, as examples only, and says e-learning cannot be relied on solely.
**Risk assessment triggers.** The FTC Safeguards Rule and the AMLR both tie content to the firm's risk assessment, so a revised risk assessment is a refresh trigger.
**Role entry triggers.** Portugal requires training immediately after hiring into an AML relevant role, and the AMLR requires the integrity assessment before people take up AML/CFT activities.

**Busy season.** Seasonal tax staff join in a short window; scheduling their security and data handling rows before system access is granted is easier than chasing completions mid season. The guide on [setting mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) covers how to justify the chosen intervals.

sections.heading: What records will an evaluator or supervisor expect from an accounting firm?

blocks.text: Expect requests for who was trained, on which content, when, and how understanding was checked, held for the longest retention period that applies. AUSTRAC's good practice example keeps a central training register and tests knowledge through quizzes or scenario discussions.

sections.heading: Which upcoming dates affect an accounting firm's matrix?

blocks.text: These dates come from the linked regulation pages, as at November 2026, and belong in the matrix as future dated rows.

items: **July 1, 2026, Australia:** accountants providing table 6 services became AUSTRAC reporting entities.
**December 10, 2026, Australia:** automated decision making transparency obligations under the Privacy Act commence.
**Within two years of July 17, 2026, Japan:** most of the APPI amending Act takes effect, adding administrative surcharges; the penalty changes apply six months after promulgation.
**July 10, 2027, EU:** the AMLR applies directly to auditors, accountants and tax advisors.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each service line, the obligations it triggers in each market and the scope decisions staff must make, then attaches assessment points to those decisions. When a source such as AUSTRAC's item 3 guidance or the AMLR changes, the affected service lines and roles can be traced from the framework. See [professional services](/industries/professional-services).

faqs.q: Do audit staff need AML training?
faqs.a: It depends on the market. Auditors are obliged entities under the EU AMLR and under Portugal's Law 83/2017, so audit staff in relevant roles need training there. In Australia, the trigger is whether the practice provides a table 6 service; audit alone is not listed, but a firm that also structures or holds client money is a reporting entity for that work.

faqs.q: Does a US tax practice with few clients still need Safeguards Rule training?
faqs.a: Yes. The 314.6 exemption for institutions holding data on fewer than 5,000 consumers switches off only paragraphs 314.4(b)(1), (d)(2), (h) and (i). Paragraph (e), including security awareness training for all personnel, still applies.

faqs.q: Is AUSTRAC's accounting starter kit enough for a growing practice?
faqs.a: Only for practices that meet its criteria: 15 or fewer personnel, mostly Australian resident individual clients and no regular high risk clients. AUSTRAC says larger practices are highly likely to face more complex risks requiring stronger controls, so they need their own role analysis rather than the kit's generic personnel policy.

faqs.q: Should seasonal and contract staff appear on the matrix?
faqs.a: Yes. The FTC Safeguards Rule applies training to all personnel, Japan's APPI counts contract, part time and dispatched workers as employees, and the AMLR extends training to persons in comparable positions. Seasonal staff often have the broadest access to client records during the busiest weeks.
